name: Charlotte
lede: The disc golf capital of the South — more championship courses per capita than anywhere. Charlotte's courses are seriously good, and most of them are free.
introParagraphs: Charlotte is the best disc golf city in the South, period. Hornets Nest is the famous one — open front nine, wooded Piedmont back nine, and a tournament history that includes the national championship. Nevin Park's Nightmare layout is the long, brutal sibling, and Kilborne, Reedy Creek, and The Scrapyard round out a top tier most metros would kill for.

Most of Charlotte's mapped courses are free, and the variety is the point: open parkland, dense Piedmont woods, water carries, and one 1,001-foot par 5 (well, that one's across the border in Kentucky). The Charlotte Disc Golf Club runs a packed tournament calendar, and the weekly doubles and tag rounds keep the competitive scene humming year-round.

New here? Start at Kilborne for the gentle intro, then face the Nightmare once you're feeling bold. For gear, Another Round Disc Golf in Plaza Midwood is the local hub — full pro shop, league nights, and a taproom.

faqs.question: How many disc golf courses are in Charlotte?
faqs.answer: There are 56 courses across the Charlotte metro, mapped and live on FindFrolf, with more added every week.

faqs.question: What's the best disc golf course in Charlotte?
faqs.answer: Hornets Nest is the most famous and most-loved — an open front nine and a wooded Piedmont back nine with tournament history. Nevin Park's Nightmare layout is the serious challenger.

faqs.question: Are Charlotte's disc golf courses free?
faqs.answer: Most are. 52 of the 56 mapped courses are free to play, and 4 are pay-to-play. Check each course page for its current green fee.

faqs.question: What's the best beginner course in Charlotte?
faqs.answer: Kilborne TPC is one of the friendliest published courses — flat, well-maintained, and fair. Work up to Reedy Creek and The Scrapyard as your lines improve.

faqs.question: Where can I buy disc golf gear in Charlotte?
faqs.answer: Another Round Disc Golf in Plaza Midwood is the local hub — full pro shop, league nights, and a taproom. Play It Again Sports on South Blvd carries new and used discs.
